status: design fixture; nothing here is loaded into the DB, the wiki or Wikibase
scope: Escalation and deferral mechanisms (what a person can do, and to whom, when a step goes wrong; where a process hands off to another body) in lexflow's curated process models and AskBench references.

type.internal appeal: Review, reconsideration, rehearing or a cure demand addressed to the same body (or its head, full board, or designee).
type.external administrative review: Review or a binding ruling by a different administrative body (the Mayor over D.C. agencies, the Texas attorney general, a Tax Commissioner, a board over a licensing official, DOJ record correction).
type.ombudsman/mediation: A neutral who tries to settle the dispute and cannot compel.
type.advisory opinion: A non-binding opinion, guideline or eligibility predetermination (some predeterminations are made binding by statute; the rung says so).
type.compliance board: A standing body that decides complaints and can order the custodian to act.
type.judicial review: Any court proceeding: petition, suit, mandamus, appeal, writ, motion to vacate.
type.oversight/inspector general: Complaint, reporting, discipline or enforcement by an oversight office or prosecutor, not a review of the individual request.
type.referral: The process hands the matter, a notice or a record to another body (the right custodian, a consultation, a records repository).
type.delegation: A body hands its authority to a designee, officer, panel or hearing office.
type.deferral to another process: The process waits on, is tolled by, or falls back to another body's decision or another process (a dispute pending elsewhere, a court order, a certificate of rehabilitation, another sealing route).

vocabulary.mandatory: true when the rung is a duty of the body, or a step the person must take to keep the next rung; false when the person may skip it. mandatory_note says which.
vocabulary.deadline: a list; each item has amount (null when the text gives no number), unit, anchor, who_must_act and kind, and, when a quote supports it, section, quote and verified.
vocabulary.body: the specific body for the jurisdiction: a proposed lexflow key (lexflow:agency, lexflow:office-type, lexflow:position, lexflow:position-type), its Wikidata item where one was found, and how it resolves when generic (resolve_by).

notes: Method. Each ladder starts from a curated process model (curated/<state>/<question>.json: actors, steps, deadlines, outcomes, cross_references, gaps) or an AskBench reference (curated_ask/<question>/<state>.json: gold sections, nuggets, steps). The remedy sections those models cite or leave out (for example Va. Code § 2.2-3713, Md. Gen. Prov. Subtitles 1A and 1B, Cal. Gov. Code § 7923.000 et seq., Tex. Gov't Code §§ 552.269-552.328, Fla. Stat. § 16.60) were read in full from the search index (lexflow/ask/index.py, open-us-law v2026.09.1). Every quote was then checked by script against that section text after whitespace, curly-quote and dash normalisation.

Grounding. A rung is fully_grounded when its mechanism quote and every trigger, deadline and supporting quote were found verbatim. All quotes verified. Rungs whose body, forum or trigger is not stated in the text carry an 'inferred' list; they are still grounded on the quote but the inference is the reader's to check.
Pinpoints are written as (a)(1)(ii) after the index citation; Virginia subsections are written (A)(5)(b). The quote, not the pinpoint, is the evidence.

Type choices. A review by the same body, its head, its full board or its designee is 'internal appeal' (New York's appeal to the entity head, Washington's two-day review, reconsideration and rehearing, Virginia's local tax appeal to the commissioner of the revenue, Ohio's three-day cure complaint, Florida's pre-suit notice). A review by a different administrative body is 'external administrative review' (the D.C. Mayor over any public body, the Texas attorney general's open records rulings and overcharge determinations, the Illinois Public Access Counselor, the Virginia Tax Commissioner over local assessments, a D.C. board over the Mayor's licensing official, California DOJ record correction). The Maryland Ombudsman, the Florida AG mediation program, North Carolina mediation and the Ohio Court of Claims mediation referral are 'ombudsman/mediation'; only the Maryland PIA Compliance Board is a 'compliance board'.
A court is the last rung of every ladder; 45 of 143 rungs are judicial. The one exclusive court is the Supreme Court of Virginia for State Corporation Commission orders (Va. Code § 12.1-39).

Silence rules found: deemed denial (VA, DC, NY, IL; Maryland treats late production as a denial), deemed exhaustion of administrative remedies (DC § 2-532(e), IL 140/9(c)), presumption that information is public when the body misses its deadline to ask the attorney general (TX § 552.302), deemed approval of a licence decision 30 days after a 'decision due' notice (VA § 2.2-4021), proposed decision deemed adopted after 100 days (CA Gov. Code § 11517), reconsideration petition deemed denied (CA § 11521), rehearing overruled by operation of law (TX § 2001.146), internal review deemed complete on the second business day (WA § 42.56.520(4)). No silence rule: California's CPRA and Florida's chapter 119 (which sets no response deadline at all).

Exhaustion. Mandatory administrative steps before court: New York's appeal to the entity head (§ 89(4)(b) reviews 'an appeal determination'), Texas licensing's motion for rehearing (§ 2001.145) and exhaustion (Occ. Code § 53.052), a requested full-board rehearing in D.C. licensing (§ 47-2853.22(i)), Ohio's three-business-day cure complaint (§ 149.43(C)(1)), and North Carolina mediation as a condition of court jurisdiction (§ 132-9(a)). Everywhere else the administrative rung is optional: D.C. Mayor review, the Maryland Ombudsman and Board (§ 4-1A-10(a)), the Illinois Public Access Counselor, the Virginia FOIA Council.

Fee disputes have a dedicated forum only in Texas (attorney general, § 552.269), Maryland (Ombudsman for fees and waivers; Compliance Board for fees over $350; notice duty for school-system fees, § 4-206(f)), Washington (court review of cost estimates, § 42.56.550(2)) and Virginia's local licence tax ladder (§ 58.1-3703.1). Elsewhere a fee dispute goes to an advisory body or to the general enforcement suit, which the rungs mark as an inference.

Hand-offs to the right custodian are explicit in Virginia (contact information for the other public body, § 2.2-3704(B)(3); the Library of Virginia for archived records, (J)), Maryland (10 working days to name the custodian, § 4-202(c)), Florida (good-faith search across the agency, § 119.07(1)(c)) and D.C. (body-worn camera requests only to MPD). Consultation with another body is an extension ground in D.C., California and Illinois.

Deferrals: Maryland extends every time limit while a dispute is before the Ombudsman or Board; North Carolina tolls all periods during mediation; Florida holds a record 30 days and then only a court may release it for disposal; the Illinois Counselor stops if the requester sues; Ohio stays Court of Claims proceedings during mediation; Virginia suspends local tax collection during an appeal; Florida and Virginia make local business receipts and licences wait on state fictitious-name filings; California bars a conviction-based licence denial after a certificate of rehabilitation or a § 1203.4-type dismissal, so the licence outcome can wait on those court processes; automatic sealing in California and Virginia falls back to a petition.

Delegation of hearings: California requires Office of Administrative Hearings judges (Gov. Code § 11502); Texas requires SOAH unless the agency has its own hearing officers (§ 2003.021); Maryland (§ 10-205) and D.C. (§ 2-1831.03(i), with appeal back to the board) make it optional; D.C. boards may also use 3-member panels; Virginia boards decide how a hearing officer sits (§ 54.1-110).

Authority attaches to posts. Statutes name the post, not the person: 'the head of the agency or a designee' (CA), 'the head, chief executive or governing body ... or the person therefor designated' (NY), 'officer for public information' (TX), 'FOIA officer' (VA, DC), 'custodian' and 'official custodian' (MD, FL), 'the appointing authority of the custodian' (MD § 4-362(e)), 'the Tax Commissioner' (VA), 'the chief judge or presiding judge' (VA § 19.2-392.7(D)). Where a statute requires a person to be identified (the names and titles or positions of those responsible for a denial, CA § 7922.540(b) and IL 140/9(a); the custodian's designee, FL § 119.07(1)(b); the agency's designated contact, VA § 2.2-4019(A)), these ladders record the post only.

Cross-references. Only 13 of 143 rungs contain, inside the quoted provision, a cross-reference (role authority, procedure, prerequisite_process, override or exception; fixtures/xref/gold_* where the section is in the gold, otherwise lexflow/law/xref.py) that resolves to another rung's section. The other rungs name the next body in words ('petition the Mayor', 'the Board', 'the Circuit Court of Leon County', 'the attorney general'), so finding ladders needs a body-mention finder (the 'mentions' relation of docs/design/entities-contacts.md), not only xref. Two cross-process links were found: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 480(c) -> Penal Code §§ 1203.4, 1203.425 (licence -> sealing) and § 480(f)(3)(D) -> Penal Code § 11126 (licence -> record correction).

Out of the corpus: court rules that set many filing limits (Rules of the Supreme Court of Virginia Part 2A, the Maryland Rules, D.C. Court of Appeals rules, California Rules of Court, Florida Rules of Appellate Procedure), the Illinois Administrative Review Law, the Florida constitutional suspension power behind § 119.10, and Md. Crim. Proc. § 10-105 (missing from the downloaded text). Rungs that depend on them say so in 'basis' or 'inferred'.

Bodies. 90 body references (85 distinct proposed keys) back the rungs: 37 specific bodies and 53 generic office types, position types or markers resolved by place, venue, profession or record holder. Privacy. No person is named. Positions are recorded as posts (lexflow:position:..., lexflow:position-type:...) with no holder and no contact details; the private-party marker is used for third parties. Victims' notices (Md. Crim. Proc. § 10-303(f)) are left out.
Design only. Nothing was written to the DB, the DokuWiki, lexipedia.wikibase.cloud, Wikidata or Govdirectory. The keys and properties referred to are proposals in docs/design/authority-ladders.md.
